text: It's King's Day, and the island's gone orange. Flags on the pier, a market on the green, somebody selling their old records out of a box. [to Gerrit] No, we're not going ashore. [dryly] I tied an orange ribbon to the aerial. Gerrit's sitting on it. That's our float in the parade.
King's Day. Everybody on the island can sell what they like today without a licence. One day a year, the whole country lives like I do. [amused] Welcome aboard, all of you.
It's Sinterklaas. Tonight's the night for presents and bad rhyming poems. I wrote one for Gerrit. [clears throat] It doesn't rhyme, and he ate it. Best review I've had all year.
Last night I put my boot by the wheelhouse stove, just in case. [deadpan] This morning there was a herring in it. I've got one suspect, and he's on the aerial looking innocent.
Sinterklaas today, and then the steamboat leaves. [wistful] I'll miss her lights at the pier. The Zeemeeuw was the second-best boat round here for three weeks, and I didn't mind once.
The steamboat's moored at the island pier. I can see her from the wheelhouse, flags all up, lights all on. [dryly] She hasn't got a licence for that either, I'd bet. We pirates recognise each other.
For a few weeks a year I've got neighbours. The steamboat, at the pier, with the saint aboard. He hasn't waved yet. [to Gerrit] Don't take it personally, he's very busy.
With the steamboat in, there's always someone on the island looking at the rooftops. Horses, they say. [amused] On my roof there's a gull, and he's not delivering anything.

Sint Maarten tonight. If you're on the island you'll see the lanterns going door to door, kids singing for sweets. [warmly] I hung a lantern on the stern. Nobody's rowing out to sing for me, but it's there.
Sint Maarten, the day for sharing your cloak with a stranger. I haven't got a cloak. I shared my sandwich with Gerrit. [dryly] He didn't ask. He never asks.
Halloween. A dark boat, no lights but one, a voice coming out of nowhere on the radio. [mock-serious] I've been a ghost story all year. Tonight I'm just in season.
Gerrit's dressed up for Halloween. He's come as a gull. [deadpan] Very convincing. I've gone as a man who didn't buy any sweets, because nobody rows out this far to knock.
I've put a string of lights up the aerial. That's the Christmas tree on the Zeemeeuw this year. [dryly] Gerrit's the angel on top. He hasn't agreed to it.
This time of year, I know some of you are listening on your own. [warmly] So am I. Two of us, then. Three with Gerrit. That's a party on this boat.

There are coloured lights in the lighthouse window that weren't there before. The keeper's done his bit. I've done mine with the spare bulbs from the engine room. Between us, the island looks almost festive.

Christmas Day. Dinner on the Zeemeeuw is a tin of something good I've been saving since summer, and a herring for Gerrit. [quietly] One chair, one mug, a full record box. Merry Christmas, from both of us.
Christmas Day. [amused] Captain, if you've got the radio on somewhere warm, Merry Christmas. Yes, from me. Don't let it go to your head.
Happy New Year from Radio Alles. Gerrit's wearing a paper hat. He let me put it on him, which is the nicest thing he's done all year. [dryly] He's already trying to eat it.
New Year's resolutions on the Zeemeeuw. Keep Opa running. Keep the needle on the record. Play the solos to the end. [mock-serious] Be nicer to the inspectors. Well... three out of four.

Another year at anchor. Nobody's moved me on, the transmitter's still standing, and you're still listening. [warmly] That's more than I'd have bet on, the day I bought this boat. Here's to the next one.
Easter. The island kids hunt for eggs in the dunes today, so I hid one on deck for Gerrit. [deadpan] He found it in four seconds and then looked at me like I'd insulted him.

Easter. The fishermen I barter with threw a chocolate egg in with the coffee last supply run. I've been saving it for today. [quietly] I'm eating it slowly, over the whole of the next record. Happy Easter.
Midsummer. The longest day there is. The lamp up at the lighthouse barely gets a turn before it's light again. [warmly] I'll stay up for the whole of it. I always do.
The shortest night of the year, and I'm going to waste none of it sleeping. Records, the deck, and the light never quite going out of the sky. [dryly] Gerrit's gone to bed. He's no romantic.
[quietly] Fifth of May. Liberation Day. People went without a free radio once, and listened in secret, at risk. Every song on this station today is played for them, and because we can.
Liberation Day. I talk about this station being free, and I mean no licence and no adverts. Today, that word means more than that. [warmly] Enjoy it. Every bit of it.
A birthday up at the lighthouse today. The keeper's. [warmly] Many happy returns, keeper, from the boat you lent your records to. [dryly] I'd sing, but you'd want them back.
It's the keeper's birthday. I'd row over with a present, but everything I own is either the station or Gerrit. So here's the next record instead. Happy birthday, keeper. It's yours anyway.
Charlie and George have a birthday today, the lighthouse cats. [fondly] Happy birthday to both. And to someone else up at the lighthouse, who shares the day. You know who you are.
Three birthdays at the lighthouse today: Charlie, George, and someone else up there I won't name on air. [to Gerrit] We're sending them a fish. No, a whole one. Don't argue.
